reason: A ratio of height (PATO_0000119) to width (PATO_0000921) above 1, with the bound excluded, like 'longer than broad' in the ratio pattern.
A hypanthium or capsule narrowed into a neck is flask-shaped: swollen below and narrowed into a neck. The 'narrow basal collar' of one French fruit does not fit and should be left unannotated.
A surface with a network of ridges or lines is reticulate. Veins that form a network with the veinlets are anastomosing, a quality of the veins themselves.
A plain negation of PATO flared. The French trunk 'sans empattement' (without spreading base) is better read as not buttressed (FLOPO:0991138).
A plain negation of PATO fringed.
A plain negation of the FLOPO value membranous.

'Leaf base narrowed and petiolelike' is a base tapering gradually into a stalk-like part, the attenuate leaf base of the floras. A petiole-like structure is not a petiole, so a petiole-present rule would be wrong.
'Without ridges' negates PATO ridged. 'Ridge' has no PO class (it was rejected as a generic part), so an entity-absence rule is not possible.
Same reading as rule C175 'indistinct': hardly visible or hardly set off from the parts around it.
'Arranged in a single row' is the definition of FLOPO uniseriate.

target: smooth (PATO_0000701) on the cells of the bearer
reason: A moss word: the leaf or propagule cells are smooth, not papillose. The quality belongs to the cells, so the bearer is the cell of the named part.
Stolon-like stems or rootstocks are ones running along the ground and rooting at the nodes, which is FLOPO creeping. They are not stolons, so a stolon-present rule would be wrong.

label: suprabasal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's arising or being located a short distance above the base of the structure that bears it. NOTE: Counterpart of FLOPO:0991002 basal; used for secondary veins arising above the leaf base (cf. FLOPO:0991202 triplinerved) and for glands and leaves.
reason: A common botanical position, especially of the lowest pair of secondary veins. No PATO or FLOPO term covers it.
A ratio of height (PATO_0000119) to width (PATO_0000921) above 1, with the bound excluded. Same as 'higher than wide'.
'Bracts readily tearing' means easily torn, a disposition to break easily, which is PATO fragile. 'Not tearing' negates it.
It gives where the part is widest but not its outline. Ovate, lanceolate and triangular parts are all widest near the base, and FLOPO ovate also requires a fully convex outline.
The counterpart of rule C344 (caulescent = stem present). The floras mean 'without an evident stem' (the stem is much reduced or below ground), and the rule should be read in that sense.

The floras' callus (a hardened swelling) has no PO class; PO plant callus (PO_0005052) is undifferentiated tissue. 'Callus' was rejected as a generic part, and the French 'sans calicule' means without an epicalyx, so the word mixes unrelated parts.

label: camphor-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having the pungent, resinous odour of camphor. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991016 sweet-scented and FLOPO:0991017 spicy-scented.
reason: A key field character of bark and leaves (e.g. Lauraceae) that is used in several floras. It fits the existing FLOPO odour classes.
A carrot-like root is a thick taproot tapering from the top, the standard example of a conical root (as opposed to fusiform or napiform).
A collar-like corona, disc or sepal is an annular rim round an axis, which is PATO ring shaped (EXACT synonym annular).
'Collective vein' names a kind of vein (an intramarginal collecting vein), not a quality. Neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for it.
Covered with bristles is PATO setose, as already noted for FLOPO:0991124 setaceous.
'Apex drawn out' and 'lobes drawn out into long narrow points' mean gradually tapering to a narrow end.
'Irregularly' loosens the shape like '±': ovate (FLOPO:0991024) with value_qualifier approximately. For 3-D seeds the value is PATO_0001891 ovate (synonym ovoid).
A knob-shaped stigma is enlarged into a rounded head, which is FLOPO head-shaped, defined for stigmas.
Nodule-bearing roots carry root nodules (rule C380: nodule = root nodule). The bacterial leaf nodules in the lamina are not root nodules, so the rule applies to roots only.

target: new: conjunction of two values (ovate FLOPO:0991024 and asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: Two values hold together: an ovate outline and an oblique (unequal-sided) base, read as asymmetrical in rule C236. It is a conjunction, not a range between two shapes.
A shape between ovate (PATO_0001891, synonym ovoid) and cylindrical (PATO_0001873), the usual compound of two shape values.
A breeding system (a process of pollination), not a quality of the flower's form. Where it comes from flowers that stay closed, FLOPO:0991176 cleistogamous already applies.
